ms.report:
The design document for HaskLedger has been completed and submitted to our GitHub repository. This document encapsulates the foundational design and framework for HaskLedger, outlining the proposed architecture, key components, and their interactions after considerating feedbacks provided by experts.
・GitHub Repository: HaskLedger GitHub
・Design Document : This document represents the finalized architectural blueprint after MLabs’ technical review. 

Commentary on Architectural Decisions

Architecture:
・The updated design defines a clear and auditable end-to-end architecture for HaskLedger.
・It integrates a typed Haskell EDSL that compiles validator logic into a deterministic Plutus Core subset, a modular off-chain/sidechain runtime built on actor pipelines for scalable execution, and a gateway service that bridges off-chain computation with Cardano Layer-1 for transaction submission and checkpointing.
・The architecture emphasizes clean separation of concerns—the EDSL governs on-chain semantics, the worker runtime handles scalable off-chain logic, and the gateway provides the policy boundary for L1 interaction.
・ Additional layers ensure reproducibility and portability across architectures (x86_64, aarch64, and riscv64 via QEMU), while preserving future extensibility for formal methods, sidechain protocols, and optional hardware acceleration.

Expected Performance Improvements:
・The design achieves predictable performance through an actor-based concurrency model with bounded queues, task sharding, and back-pressure control.
・Critical operations such as cryptographic primitives and data serialization are optimized through deterministic Rust FFI modules, delivering measurable speedups while maintaining reproducibility and type safety.
・Explicit performance metrics—boot-to-ready time, p95 latency, throughput under load, and STM contention rates—are defined and linked to reproducible benchmarks.

ms.report:
HaskLedger does not alter Cardano’s consensus rules, block frequency or aggregate network capacity. What it demonstrably improves is the amount of Cardano’s fixed block execution budget consumed by each equivalent validation. Lower resource consumption allows more equivalent validating transactions to fit within the same protocol-defined block budget and reduces the execution component of transaction fees.
All benchmark code, baseline contracts, methodology, raw measurements and reproduction instructions are publicly available in the updated repository:

The benchmark can be independently reproduced through the documented haskledger-bench and PlutusTx baseline commands. The harness exits with an error if a validator rejects the positive-case input, preventing results from being generated from silently failing scripts.
The earlier review stated that it was not possible to assess whether the throughput and efficiency acceptance criterion had been met. It is now possible to assess it directly, quantitatively and independently.
The missing evidence is no longer presented as an assumption, projection or narrative claim. It is measured against the standard Cardano Haskell toolchain, derived from the applicable block execution limits, published in the repository and reproducible by the reviewer.
We therefore respectfully request that the milestone be reassessed against the precise acceptance criterion and the new evidence supplied.
